prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1383; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Records show long-standing treatment for the same condition before the crash; most of the current complaints come from it.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim was reported by phone and the claimant described a rear-end collision at a traffic signal. The claimant is not represented by an attorney and has been told how the claim process works.

Entry 2: The policy lists the driver of the insured vehicle as a named driver, and that driver's coverage was confirmed as in force at the time of the reported loss.

Entry 3: The police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene. No independent witnesses to the impact itself have been identified so far.

Entry 4: Scene photos were received and show some of the damage described in the claimant's account. The overall damage appears mostly consistent with the described impact, and the vehicle has been scheduled for a full inspection.

Entry 5: The claimant reports a wrist fracture from the collision. The reported injury is plausible for a crash of this type, and an authorization for medical records has been requested.

Entry 6: Medical records were received. They show treatment for the wrist that ran somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, and the claimant's physician notes were requested for clarification.

Entry 7: Prior medical records show long-standing treatment for the same wrist condition before the reported crash. Most of the current complaints appear to relate to that earlier condition, and this is being reviewed.

Entry 8: A neighbor contacted the office and stated the vehicle appeared damaged some weeks before the claimed loss date. No prior damage to the vehicle is recorded in our files, and the statement has been noted for follow-up.

Entry 9: The claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation so far, with no changes to the sequence of events. The claimant's account has been recorded in full in the file.

Entry 10: Claim remains open pending the vehicle inspection, the neighbor follow-up, and review of the prior medical records. A status update will be sent to the claimant once these items are complete.
